key_insight: RadKev-27B improved task-averaged accuracy over Kev-27B by 4.9 percentage points and outperformed hosted decision models and a same-size LLM on radiology tasks.
clinical_relevance: Open-weight deployment could keep patient data within an institution while supporting fixed-choice radiology tasks, pending local validation.
method: Fine-tuned Kev-27B and Kev-9B on 36,109 public radiology records.
Evaluated 14,142 held-out questions across 15 report-reading, diagnosis/classification, and knowledge tasks.
Compared against base Kev models, two hosted decision models, and Qwen3.8-27B.
evidence_signal: The primary accuracy gain was 4.9 percentage points (95% CI 3.8–6.2); on a 1,675-question comparison, RadKev-27B had 132-fold lower latency than the reasoning LLM (128 ms vs 16.9 s).
watch_item: Held-out benchmark performance does not establish clinical safety or workflow benefit; local validation is needed before deployment.
paper_title: RadKev: An Open-Weight Decision Model for Radiology
